rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about a fading autumn. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: The leaves in golden hues do fall,
A dance of days that slowly wane,
The crispness in the air does call,
To frost where summer's warmth was lain.
The golden leaves do gently fall, adieu,
In twilight's embrace, they drift away,
The once-bounteous trees now stark and true,
Proclaim the fading light of day by day.
The leaves in gold and russet fall, doth say,
Each one a whisper to the crisp, cool air,
The sun doth bathe them in a fading light,
Till night claims all, and winter's breath doth draw near.
The leaves doth fall in golden showers, a-slow,
And bid the year with sighing farewells,
The once-robust now withers cold and low,
A somber harbinger of waning spells.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about lost love. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: In shadows of the fading light you went,
From hearts that still could hear your gentle tread,
No echo now remains, our love is spent,
Save in the memories where we used to tread.
In fading eyes a once-luminous flame,
Now dimmed and cold, as erstwhile hearts did flame,
No word, no sign, no trace of what we were,
Left only in the memory, sad and small.
In shadows deep where once our spirits danced,
Now echoes lone a silence, void, and cold,
Our laughter fades, like fading morning glances,
Till heart to heart no longer feels, but tells.
In twilight's shadow, where the ghostly leaves sigh,
My heart still whispers oft thy name, I pine,
No spring returns to bloom where thou didst lie,
But wintry gloom doth wither love's fair prime.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about the passage of time. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: Hours like leaves on ancient trees do fall,
Day by day, in time's unending scroll,
Sunsets paint the sky with gold and violet,
Night succeeds, to claim the day's release.
The sunset paints the sky in golden hue,
As hours unheedingly do pass and go,
The twilight comes to claim the day's last view,
As shadows lengthen, time's soft grip does show.
Hours like leaves in autumn, once fallen, are lost,
Days like doves in twilight, are gone in a trice,
Weeks like waves at sundown, recede and take boast,
Months like moonlit dreams fade, in the dark of thenice
The sun doth rise, then sets in silent doom,
Each day a stone in time's unyielding stream,
The leaves in spring, in autumn's frosty gloom,
Do fall, to rise no more till verdant dream.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about a winter night. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: In twilight's fade where day and night交接处，
Snow whispers hush upon the pine,
The moon casts shadows in the glen,
While winds doth moan in solemn chime。
Snow muffles earth in quiet slumber deep,
While moonbeams dance upon the windows' sheen,
The world in white, in frosty breath doth keep,
A watchful vigil o'er the wintereen.
Silent the night, where snow doth softly lie,
By moonlight gilding frost upon the ground,
The world in hush beneath the wintry sky,
No sound but breath upon the frosty air.
The moon doth shine with frosted light, so pale,
Upon the frost, where twigs do stand at attention,
The silent air with ice doth hold its breath,

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about spring rain. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: Spring rain whispers in soft measured time,
Gentle upon the petals new and prime,
It sings a song of life's rebirth and bloom,
In every drop, the promise it renews.
Spring rain falls softly, nature's steady beat,
Misting the earth with life's sustaining thread,
In gentle drops it whispers to the seed,
Awakening slumber in the winter's heat.
Softly the spring rain falls, a whispering thread,
Washing the world clean, its pale green handspread,
New buds uncurl under the moistening touch,
Life breathes again as winter's grip relaxes,
Spring rain falls soft on budding leaves,
Awakening sleep with liquid streams,
In gentle showers it seems to breathe,
Life under skies that wearily gleam.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about an old friend. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: In days of old, our spirits did entwine,
With laughter bright and shared dreams unconfined,
But time, a river ever wide and deep,
Doth part us now where once we did weep.
In misty glens we used to roam, my friend,
Where shadows loiter and the wildwood's breath
Doth whisper secrets of aearlier days,
Now distant echoes in the quiet west.
Our paths did long ago diverge, we part,
Yet still thy voice in memory I recall,
A friend so dear, though time may shift and shift,
Thy laughter's echo still my heart doth enthral.
In twilight of years, our paths did cross again,
Memories like wine, grew richer as we drank,
Together we laughed at life's soft irony,
Parting hence, old friend, with nod and thank.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about the moon. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: Silvered moon doth high悬在空中，
Guides night's sleep with gossamer touch，
Stars fade as her light swayают，
Solves all darkness in lunar clutch.
The moon doth rise in silent, mystic grace,
Its silver light doth softly, gently pour,
On hills and dales, a spell that dreams may chase,
In twilight's arms, where only shadows soar.
The moon doth wax and wane in silent grace,
A luminous round in the velvet sky,
Its silver light doth bathe the world in peace,
While shadows lengthen as the night draws nigh.
Silent moon doth hang in the twilight's embrace,
Its cold light bathes the world in silver grace,
Then whispers fade as dawn its edge does trace,
And moon withdraws to dreams within the space.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about a distant city. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: In misty dawn's embrace, afar I spy,
A city sleeps, in silvery light arrayed,
Its spires reach high where shadows softly lie,
Beneath the moon, in tranquil dreams arrayed.
In misty veils the city whispers far,
Its spires in twilight's grasp do bravely stand,
A dream of light where shadows softly bar,
And noise of life in tranquil silence glides.
In misty veils, afar I spy thy towers,
Gilded spires in sunlight, silent, proud, and grand,
Thy streets with shadows weave in even hours,
A city dreams beneath the watchful land.
In twilight's hue her spires doth wear, Berlin,
With history's ghosts in silent wheel,
Where shadows sweep o'er boulevards old,
In whispers of the past, Berlin, Berlin.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about childhood memory. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: In fields of green where buttercups did gleam,
I ran, a laughing sprite, 'neath azure sky,
Each daisy chain a circlet for my dream,
Where time stood still, in memory's embrace.
In fields of green beneath the azure sky,
I gathered flowers where my grandmother'd lie,
Her hands so warm, her love a honeyed flood,
Beneath the shade where whispered winds did brood.
In fields of golden wheat I used to play,
Where sunbeams danced and shadows lightly swayed;
Each blade a sword, each stalk a xếp of knight,
In dreams of green I lost the brightly-bled.
In fields of green where daisies danced with breeze,
I ran unbound by time or worry's lease,
Each moment pure, a memory untold,
In sunlit days that sang where I did roam.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about a burning candle. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: In votive flame that dances with the night,
Its golden tears upon the wick do fall,
Until the core of self it doth enshrine,
And with a hiss, in sighing silence, falls.
A flame that flickers, weak or strong, doth stand,
In shadows cast, its light a fragile thing;
Yet as it burns, itself it slowly kills,
Till nothing left remains but cold, blackening.
A flame doth dance with liquid gold, so bright,
Its breath kept steady by the air's soft touch,
Yet warmth and light shall soon to shadows bring,
Till waxen tears in silence sob and clutch.
A flame that dances in the dark, it glows,
Its waxen tears in flickering streams descend,
But soon its fuel spent, it willno more bestow
Its light, nor be than dust and shadow send.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about the mountain wind. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: Through mountain passes whispers swift and free,
Its breath a dance of chill upon the skin,
In valleys echoes low a mournful sigh,
As shadows lengthen with the setting sun.
Mountain wind whispers, cold and keen,
Through the pines it sighs, deep and deep,
Echoes in the valley green,
Chilling the breeze where shadows steep.
The mountain wind doth whisper, soft and low,
Through hollows deep where ancient pines alternate,
It sings a ballad of the misty mow,
In crevices where shadows dare to start.
The mountain wind doth moan and sigh,
With gusts that dance upon the peak,
It whispers secrets in the night,
As shadows play where none may speak.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about a quiet garden. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: In still nook where shadows softly slumber,
Flowers nod to breezes that barely stir,
A peaceful hush lies over every bower,
Where time itself seems slow in twilight's turn.
In silent nook where shadows softly play,
No sound but whispers of the zephyr's breath,
A rose reclines 'neath twilight's tender sway,
In calm repose where time and cares takeflight.
In silent nook where shadows softly play,
The rose entwines its fragrant, tender way,
No noisy breeze to stir each leafy crest,
But hush reigns where only peace is lest.
In silent bower where shadows play,
The whispering breeze does gently stray,
Around each flower in delicate array,
The quietude doth hold its mystic sway.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about the first snow. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: First snowflakes dance in twilight's gray,
Adorning barren boughs with frosty lace,
The world in hush beneath the winter's play,
Silent, stark, in purity's embrace.
The hush of snow whispers, a silent refrain,
Adorning earth's cloak, in soft, unyielding sheen,
A world transformed, in frosty, crystal chains,
White peace descends, where twilight's edge is seen.
First flakes descend in silent, dancing play,
Soft veils of white upon the night do fall,
Each crystal star a gift from heaven's eye,
Adorning earth in silver, quiet, small.
The silent flurries kiss the thawing ground,
In hushed embrace they lay their snowy spoon,
The world in white, a blanket newly wound,
Night's breath in frost, the dawn's first frosted crown.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about a river's journey. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: The river winds through tranquil meadows wide,
To where the mountains loom in twilight's shade,
Then dashes down steep banks to valleys wide,
In foaming surge, its journey's rapture made.
The river winds through glades and shady dells,
Its murmuring voice a soothing lullaby,
Then swift it flows o'er pebbles, clear, and knells
Its silver song as daylight fades to night.
Through winding banks the river softly flows,
Its silver current mirrors heaven's bow,
O'er stones and pastures it unwinds its voice,
In murmurs gentle as a lover's vow.
From mountain springs to plains it winds its way,
In sunlight glimmers water cold and clear,
Through valleys flows beneath the leafy shade,
Then meets the sea in tranquil murmurs dear.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about solitude. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: In quiet chambers where no voice intrudes,
The mind with former thoughts repeals alone,
No friendly breath the silence does confute,
But shadows dance where none may breathe a lone.
In quietude where whispers softly play,
No echo answers but the silent sky,
Alone I dwell with thoughts that gently sway,
In solitude, where no one eyes do spy.
In silent nook where shadows softly fall,
Each thought does run in sweetest, calmest thrall,
Unto the stars that watch o'er solitude,
Where none but time and stillness may enthrall.
In quiet chambers of the mind un-shared,
Where whispers of the self in silence bide,
No echo answers to its naked word,
But close the doors upon the world outside.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about a summer storm. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: Thunder roars, then silence, as dark clouds gather,
Raindrops pitter-patter, in quick, relentless measure,
Lightning splits the night, a fierce, white-blushing racer,
Hush falls, the storm's wild dance begins to waver.
Thunder roars, a summer night's unrest,
Rain drums fierce upon the plain below,
Lightning flashes, nature's fiery feast,
Heralding rain's return from highen'd woe.
Thunder roars in deepening twilight's shade,
An ominous cloud descends from heaven's glade,
The rain begins in sudden, driving flood,
As lightning splits the night in jagged blade.
The thunder roars, the skies a darkening shroud,
The lightning flashes, nature's lance well-aimed,
The rain descends in angry, icy showers,
The storm.icons its threatening, awful claim.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about the harvest. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: The golden fields in swathes of amber fall,
A harvest bold, where labor's sweat has been,
Each ear a testament to sun and stall,
In bounty gathered where the crops have been.
The golden fields bow low in the cool breeze,
ripe fruit hung heavy on the fruitful trees;
The scythes stand idle, the barns are well filled,
and autumn joys make the laborers smile.
The golden fields in twilight's gentle glow,
Reap vengeance on the laboring scythe's wide throw,
Each ear a testament to sun and rain,
In bounteous sheaves they nod, the harvest's chain.
The golden fields in swathes of amber lie,
Reapers with bounteous sheaves in joyful throng,
The sun a burning eye that doth them supply,
Harvest of crops in thankfulness they sung.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about a sleeping child. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: In slumber's grasp, the child doth rest, so still,
Each breath a whisper in the quiet air,
Dreams weave their magic in her closed eyelill,
Untroubled by the world, she finds her lair.
In slumber's hold, soft breaths do gently blow,
Eyes closed tight where dreams in darkness grow,
No noise intrudes, in quiet's deep domain,
Till morn summons with gentle, rising strain.
In slumber's sweetest hold, he lies so still,
Dreaming through closed lids, as night unwinds,
A breath soft whispers through the silence chill,
In peaceful arms, a quiet world he finds.
In slumber's embrace, soft and still he lies,
Dreams woven round his gently closed eyes;
The world beyond his sheltered senses fades,
Till morn in whispers calls the slumberer'srades.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about the northern star. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: In icy skies the northern star does shine,
A guiding light through winter's darkest night,

Endures in heaven, ever bright, delight.

Its light unchanging in the starry urns.

Guiding lost souls with its eternal light,

In northern skies, a beacon steady glows,

immutable light, through ages it streameth.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about a ruined tower. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: On crumbling stones the melancholy sun doth shine,
In whispering winds its tales of yore it still doth tell,
An echo of glory where once proud knights had been,
Now lone and ghostly, in shadows, it doth steadfast dwell.
Amidst the whispering grasses lay the tower,
Its stones half-hidden in the sun's gold light,
Gone are its proud days in the keen blower,
Now echoes only where its former height.
Risen in splendor once, now shadows lie,
Its walls doth whisper tales of yore, and die,
In ruin crashed it leaves its pride behind,
Save where the ivy glitters like unpruned vine.
In ruins doth the tower still stand,
Its spire a shadow 'gainst the sky,
Mute witness to a bygone land,
Where once it held the heavens high.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about morning mist. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: Morning mist doth whisper, soft and shy,
Enveloping hills in diaphanous veils,

Silent shadows held by pale prevails.

Enveloping the earth in gentle, cool repose,

Revealing not, but shrouding in a mystic close.
Morning mist doth whisper soft, obscure the sun's first light,
Enveloping the world in veils of translucid white.
A hush descends as nature takes a breath anew,
In misty gloaming, shadows dance where none are nigh.
Morning mist doth rise in softest gray,
Enveloping earth in gentle veil,
Sunlight struggles, shoots its beams in play,
Fingered through vapor, wins its way.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about the tide. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: The tide doth ebb and flow beneath the moon's soft gaze,
In measured rhythm, governed by the lunar rays,
Each surge a pulse, in darkness or in sun's embrace,
A dance eternal, under night or day's pale face.
The wave doth kiss the shore, then sighing falls,
Drawn by the moon's invisible, compelling hand,
The sands reclaim their quiet holds, enthralls,
Ere night in silver tears the darkness charted.
The tide does ebb and flow, a gentle dance,
By moon's soft grace, in rhythmic, measured beat,

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about a nightingale. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: In twilight's hush the nightingale doth sing,
A melody so sweet, so clear, so strong,
No earthly strain can touch its soft regret,
Till morn's first light its song shall fade, unmingling.
In twilight's hush the nightingale does sing,
Her song so sweet 'neath starlit heaven's throng,
No earthly minstrel such a note can bring,
O'er verdant boughs her liquid music flings.
In twilight's embrace, the nightingale doth sing,
A melody so sweet, it seems to bring
The very stars to dance upon the night,
Till morn shall wake and steal its magic light.
In twilight's hush, where shadows softly play,
The nightingale doth sing her sweetest lay,
No human ear her melody can stay,
But in the night, her song doth fill the may.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about falling leaves. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: Fading leaves in twilight's gentle hold,
Dance from trees with autumn's whispered stride,
Crimson, gold, and amber, falling still,
Soft caress of seasons' end, we bide.

Each whispering, "Winter draws nigh,"
The golden dancer from branch to ground,
Till silence rests where once they bounded.
Falling leaves in gentle cascade,
Crimson, gold, and amber blend;
Drift and whirl, then softly lands,
Muffling earth with feathered tend.

Each a leaflet singing under autumn's breath,
Tumbling, turning, to the earth they bind,
Whispering tales as winter draws its breath.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about the desert. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: The sandy wastes where sunbeams dance in light,
Unyielding dunes that stretch in hushed repose,
A whispered breeze the vast silence takes flight,
And shadows grow where no moon dare disclose.
The sun-blazed sands in golden waves unfold,
Where scarce a blade ofWithered grass is rolled,

Where sun's relentless dance never finds ease,
In sands that shift with time's slow tease,
Echoes fade where once life did dispose.
The sun doth blare in fiery noon's embrace,
Beneath the vast and empty azure dome,
No shade to soothe the arid, thirsty space,
Where sands in golden waves doth ebb and come.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about a lighthouse. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.

Rescuing ships from ruthless, wrathful waves;

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about twilight. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: The day doth fade to twilight's hushful tone,
Soft shadows stretch across the waning light,
The sky in hues of purple and of gold,
Doth close the day's record 'gainst night's bright fight.
The day doth fade in twilight's gentle shade,
Where shadows lengthen as the sun retreats,
The sky ambers, pinks, in rosy state,
Till darkness claims the realm of light's retreat.
The sun descends in golden afterglow,
Its rays retreat in tender, fading light,
The dusk receives the world in somber glow,
As shadows stretch and twilight's peace takes flight.
The sun descends in golden afterglow,
Its rays in twilight's embrace doth drown,
The world in softest hues it slowly throw,

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about an empty road. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: An empty road stretches to the fading light,
In silent stretch where none but shadows dare,
The moonrise whispers to the lonely night,
And echoes softly in the crisp, cold air.
An empty road stretches to twilight's gray,
In silence it waits under moon's cool eye,
No echo with step breaks the night's lullay,
Save for wind's soft sigh where none souls reply.
An empty road lies quiet, dust unbroken,
By pale moonlight, where no footprints are taken,
The silence stretched, a heavy, breathless darkness,
Until the dawn breaks, and day's cold hand shaken.
An empty road stretches to twilight's embrace,
In silent hollows where none dare to trace,
No footprints mar its solitude's cold space,
Till moonlight weeps upon the unyielding base.

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about the orchard in bloom. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
candidates: Bare boughs in spring now bud and burst with bloom,
Soft petals catch the sun's first waking ray,
A fragrant mist doth fill each tranquil room,
Where orchard sweet in blossom holds its sway.
In boughs athwart the sapphire sky they stretch,
With bloom erectile, pearls of pink and white,
Where zephyrs breathe on them a perfumed breath,
And blush them deeper where the sunbeams light.
Blossoms kiss each branch in rosy hue,
And sweetest scent the quiet air does breathe,
Amongst the boughs a gentle breeze doth dew,
Soft shadows dance where petals gently weave.
In bloom the orchard stands in rosy hue,
Each bud a promise, soft and sweetly swears,

rows.brief: Write a single four-line stanza (a quatrain) about the harbor. Use strict iambic pentameter (ten syllables per line) and an ABAB rhyme scheme. Output only the four lines, nothing else.
